subject: ClearHealth: Request for subprocessors roster and data egress mapping
messages:
From: Claire Thompson <security@clearhealth.com>
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@clearhealth.com>
Date: 2028-05-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: subprocessors roster + data egress mapping

Hi Vivek,

We’re finalizing our vendor risk assessment for the ClearHealth integration. Can you share Redwood’s current list of subprocessors (names, country, purpose) and a high-level egress/dataflow map showing where customer data may travel for US and EU tenants? Our security team specifically needs to confirm: 

- Any subprocessors that have access to raw production request logs or full request payloads (not anonymized).
- Whether any of those subprocessors process data in India, Russia, or other high-risk jurisdictions.
- The KMS/HSM providers used for tenant key management and whether keys are customer-controlled or Redwood-managed.

We’re working to close an internal compliance gate next week; a spreadsheet and any attestation or SOC2 linkage would be ideal. If there are DPA amendments or an addendum required to restrict cross-border routing, please flag that.

Thanks,
Claire Thompson
Security Program Manager
ClearHealth
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Claire Thompson <security@clearhealth.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-23T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: subprocessors roster + data egress mapping

Hi Claire — thanks for the note and the clear ask. I’m attaching our current roster (CSV) for your intake team and a quick summary below. Naomi and Kim are looped in for evidence and any DPA redlines.

Top-level answers:
- Access to raw production request payloads: Very limited. Only two operational subprocessors have read access to full request logs for debugging purposes: CloudOps LogStore (US) and TelemetryFix (US/EU). We maintain strict ACLs and short retention on those logs.
- Processing in India/Russia: No production processing occurs in Russia. A small percentage of support tooling (anonymized metrics collection) uses vendors with engineering in India — they do NOT receive raw request payloads.
- KMS/HSM: We use customer-managed keys for Private deployments (bring-your-own-key via KMS) and Redwood-managed HSM-backed keys for Hosted customers. Full attestation for HSM partners is attached.

Requested attachments: redwood_subprocessor_roster_20280523.csv (attached) — columns: vendor, country, purpose, data_access_level, logs_access, sop_link.

Next steps: Naomi will follow up with the KMS/HSM attestation and SOC2 mapping. If you need a DPA amendment to lock routing for EU tenants, we can provide a scoped addendum and start DocuSign.

Best,
Vivek
Head of Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_subprocessor_roster_20280523.csv (xlsx/csv stub)
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Claire Thompson <security@clearhealth.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-24T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: subprocessors roster + data egress mapping

On Wed, May 23, 2028 at 11:03 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Claire — thanks for the note and the clear ask. I’m attaching our current roster (CSV) for your intake team and a quick summary below. Naomi and Kim are looped in for evidence and any DPA redlines.

Thanks Vivek — adding additional detail from privacy/security: 

1) Evidence and control posture
- SOC 2: Redwood’s SOC 2 Type II report (control mapping pages) is available to customers under NDA. We can provide the report or a clean-room summary depending on your vendor intake policy.
- KMS/HSM attestation: see attached kms_attestation_summary.pdf — partner names and FIPS-level info included. Hosted customers use Redwood-managed HSM with tenant partitioning; Private customers may bring KMS keys (we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault).

2) Data routing & residency options
- EU residency: We offer a pinned-region option for EU tenants (data stays within EU regions and EU-resident subprocessors). For Hosted EU customers, we route through our EU-only stack; for Dedicated, we can provide on-prem or VPC-only deployment.
- Fallbacks: We do maintain a fallback routing policy (e.g., temporary cross-region failover). If you require strict no-failover routing, we’ll need a routing addendum in the DPA.

3) Logs and debugging
- Raw payload access is tightly limited, redacted by default, and logged. Operational access is gated via just-in-time elevation and requires approvals documented in our ops playbook.

Action items I propose:
- We’ll provide SOC2 under NDA (please confirm preferred sharing method).
- If ClearHealth requires an explicit no-cross-border routing guarantee, let us know so we can draft the DPA addendum (we’ll surface implementation constraints and any cost delta).

Attachment: kms_attestation_summary.pdf

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Claire Thompson <security@clearhealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-25T10:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: subprocessors roster + data egress mapping

Hi Naomi/Vivek — appreciated, this helps a lot. Two quick asks before we close our intake: 

1) Can you share SOC2 under NDA by EOD Wednesday? Our legal team prefers a secure link; DocuSign or a secure S3 presigned link is fine.
2) We need a scoped routing addendum for EU tenants that: (a) prevents automatic cross-region failover for EU-resident data unless we authorize it, and (b) enumerates which subprocessors are allowed to touch EU data. Please draft a short addendum and indicate any operational impact or fees.

Also — please confirm the retention window for debug logs that include request context and whether we can request on-demand redaction exports for our tenant.

If you can provide the SOC2 link and a draft addendum, we’ll fast-track approval.

Best,
Claire Thompson
Security Program Manager
ClearHealth
